claim: GeoCas9 is a thermophilic Cas9 from Geobacillus stearothermophilus with DNA cleavage function up to 85 °C.
source: The emergence of the thermophilic GeoCas9, with DNA cleavage function up to 85 °C, can expand CRISPR technology to higher temperature regimes and stabilities (Belato et al., 2022b; Harrington et al., 2017)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work (Belato et al., 2022b; Harrington et al., 2017)

claim: SpyCas9 originates from the mesophilic Streptococcus pyogenes.
source: The SpyCas9, which originates from the mesophilic Streptococcus pyogenes, as well as GeoCas9, are both effectors of Type-II CRISPR systems.
evidence: Established scientific knowledge about SpyCas9 origin

claim: Type II-A SpyCas9 has been the most used Cas enzyme, including in ongoing clinical trials.
source: Interestingly, the Type II-A SpyCas9 has been by far the most used Cas enzyme, including in ongoing clinical trials (Zhang et al., 2023; Li et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to recent literature (Zhang et al., 2023; Li et al., 2023)

claim: GeoCas9 belongs to the Type II-C class of Cas9 homologs.
source: But Cas9 homologs of the Type II-C class, such as Neisseria meningitis (NmeCas9) and Campylobacter jejuni (CjeCas9), to which GeoCas9 belongs, have been validated for mammalian genome editing (Harrington et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2016)
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work (Harrington et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2016)

claim: GeoCas9 utilizes a 5'NNNNCRAA-3' protospacer adjacent motif (PAM).
source: GeoCas9 utilizes a guide RNA (gRNA) to localize and unwind a double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) target after recognition of its 5'NNNNCRAA-3' protospacer adjacent motif (PAM; Harrington et al., 2017; Jinek et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work (Harrington et al., 2017; Jinek et al., 2012)

claim: The Rec lobe of Cas9 is responsible for orienting the RNA:DNA hybrid and adjacent nuclease domains into their active conformations.
source: The Rec lobe of Cas9 is responsible for orienting the RNA:DNA hybrid, as well as the adjacent nuclease domains, into their active conformations (Palermo et al., 2018; Dagdas et al., 2017; Mir et al., 2018; Jiang et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior work (Palermo et al., 2018; Dagdas et al., 2017; Mir et al., 2018; Jiang et al., 2015)

claim: GeoCas9 is 281 residues shorter than SpyCas9.
source: The high thermal stability and more compact size of GeoCas9 (it is 281 residues shorter than SpyCas9)
evidence: Direct comparison of protein sizes stated in the manuscript

claim: AAV vectors have cargo capacities of approximately 4.7 kb.
source: can be especially important for in vivo delivery applications, since promising viral vectors (i.e. adeno-associated virus, AAV) have cargo capacities of ~4.7 kb (Wu et al., 2010)
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work (Wu et al., 2010)

claim: AAV cargo capacity prevents SpyCas9-gRNA packaging into a single AAV vector but permits 'all-in-one' delivery of GeoCas9-gRNA.
source: which prevents SpyCas9-gRNA packaging into a single AAV vector but permits 'all-in-one' delivery of GeoCas9-gRNA (Mir et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work (Mir et al., 2018)

claim: The X-ray crystal structure of GeoRec2 was solved at 1.49 Å resolution.
source: We engineered constructs of the GeoRec1 (136 residues, 16 kDa) and GeoRec2 (212 residues, 25 kDa) subdomains and solved the X-ray crystal structure of GeoRec2 at 1.49 Å
evidence: Direct experimental result reported in the manuscript

claim: The GeoRec2 X-ray crystal structure aligns with the AlphaFold model with an RMSD of 1.03 Å.
source: which aligns remarkably well with the structure of the GeoRec2 domain within the AlphaFold model (RMSD 1.03 Å)
evidence: Structural comparison data from the manuscript

claim: The GeoRec2 X-ray crystal structure aligns with the cryo-EM structure of GeoCas9 with an RMSD of 1.10 Å.
source: and new cryo-EM structure of GeoCas9 (RMSD 1.10 Å, Figure 1A).
evidence: Structural comparison data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 1A

claim: GeoRec2 and SpyRec3 have only 22% sequence identity but are highly structurally similar with an RMSD of 2.00 Å.
source: Despite only 22% sequence identity, the structure of SpyRec3 and GeoRec2 are highly similar (RMSD 2.00 Å, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Structural comparison data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: 1H-15N amide and 1H-13CH3 ILV-methyl NMR spectra of GeoRec overlay well with those of its individual subdomains.
source: 1H-15N amide and 1H-13CH3 Ile, Leu, and Val (ILV)-methyl NMR spectra (Figure 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 3) of GeoRec overlay very well with those of its individual subdomains
evidence: NMR spectroscopy data from the manuscript with reference to figures

claim: The linkage of subdomains within the full-length GeoRec polypeptide does not alter their individual folds.
source: suggesting that the linkage of subdomains within the full-length GeoRec polypeptide does not alter their individual folds.
evidence: Inference drawn from NMR spectroscopy data showing spectral overlap

claim: GeoRec1 has a melting temperature (Tm) of approximately 34 °C.
source: circular dichroism (CD) thermal unfolding profiles of GeoRec1 (Tm ~34 °C)
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript

claim: GeoRec2 has a melting temperature (Tm) of 61.50 °C.
source: and GeoRec2 (Tm = 61.50 °C) are distinct and occur as separate events in the unfolding profile of GeoRec (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 1—figure supplement 4

claim: K267 and R332 residues in GeoRec2 are less than 5 Å from the bound RNA:DNA hybrid based on the AlphaFold2 model.
source: Based on the AlphaFold2 model of GeoCas9, both of these residues are <5 Å from the bound RNA:DNA hybrid and were predicted to interface with the nucleic acids directly (Figure 2A/B).
evidence: Structural prediction from AlphaFold2 model with reference to Figure 2A/B

claim: A cryo-EM structure of GeoCas9 confirmed the interaction between K267 and the gRNA.
source: A new experimental cryo-EM structure of GeoCas9 confirmed the interaction between K267 and the gRNA, but does not report a<5 Å interaction of R332 with the gRNA (Shen et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citation to recent cryo-EM structure (Shen et al., 2024)

claim: The K267E GeoRec2 variant is sequentially and structurally similar to the K526E site in SpyCas9 within the evoCas9 system.
source: The K267E GeoRec2 variant is sequentially and structurally similar to a specificity enhancing site in SpyCas9 (K526E), within the evoCas9 system (Casini et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work (Casini et al., 2018)

claim: The SpyCas9 K526E mutation substantially reduced off-target activity alone.
source: The SpyCas9 K526E mutation substantially reduced off-target activity alone, but was even more effective in conjunction with three other single-point mutations in SpyRec3 (Casini et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work (Casini et al., 2018)

claim: The R332A GeoRec2 variant resembles the R691A mutation in HiFi SpyCas9.
source: The R332A GeoRec2 variant also resembles one mutation within a high-specificity SpyCas9 variant, an early iteration of HiFi SpyCas9 called HiFi Cas9-R691A (Vakulskas et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior work (Vakulskas et al., 2018)

claim: Chemical shift perturbations and line broadening caused by K267E and R332A mutations are highly localized to the mutation sites.
source: Consistent with experiments using GeoRec2 alone, chemical shift perturbations and line broadening are highly localized to the mutation sites. (Figure 2C–F).
evidence: NMR chemical shift perturbation data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 2C–F

claim: Wild-type GeoRec2 has a Tm of approximately 62 °C.
source: The Tm of WT GeoRec2 is ~62 °C, consistent with the Tm of the full-length GeoCas9
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript

claim: K267E GeoRec2 has a decreased Tm of approximately 55 °C.
source: while that of K267E GeoRec2 was decreased to ~55 °C.
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript

claim: R332A GeoRec2 maintains a Tm of approximately 62 °C but undergoes a smaller unfolding event near 40 °C.
source: Though the R332A GeoRec2 Tm remains ~62 °C, this variant underwent a smaller unfolding event near 40 °C before completely unfolding.
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript

claim: Both K267E and R332A mutations are destabilizing to GeoRec2.
source: These data suggest that despite small structural perturbations, both mutations are destabilizing to GeoRec2
evidence: Inference drawn from CD spectroscopy data showing altered thermal stability

claim: Order parameters (S2) for GeoRec2 are globally elevated, suggesting ps-ns motions arise primarily from global tumbling.
source: However, unlike GeoHNH, S2 values for GeoRec2 are globally elevated, suggesting that the ps-ns motions of this subdomain arise primarily from global tumbling of the protein in solution.
evidence: NMR relaxation data analysis from the manuscript

claim: Evidence of μs-ms motions is observed in 17 residues within the GeoRec2 core.
source: Evidence of μs-ms motions (i.e. curved relaxation dispersion profiles) is observed in 17 residues within the GeoRec2 core, spanning its interfaces to Rec1 and HNH (Figure 3A and B, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: CPMG relaxation dispersion NMR data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 3A and B

claim: μs-ms motions are completely absent from GeoHNH.
source: Such motions are completely absent from GeoHNH
evidence: Comparison with prior NMR data on GeoHNH

claim: The global kex for WT GeoRec2 is 147±41 s–1.
source: An analysis of chemical exchange rates, kex, derived from dual-field CPMG relaxation dispersion show a global kex for WT GeoRec2 of 147±41 s–1.
evidence: CPMG relaxation dispersion NMR data from the manuscript

claim: The K267E mutation shifts the globally fitted kex to 376±89 s–1.
source: The K267E mutation, which directly contacts the nucleic acids, shifts the globally fitted kex to 376±89 s–1
evidence: CPMG relaxation dispersion NMR data from the manuscript

claim: The R332A variant maintains a global kex similar to WT GeoRec2 at 142±28 s–1.
source: while the R332A variant maintains a global kex similar to that of WT GeoRec2 (142±28 s–1)
evidence: CPMG relaxation dispersion NMR data from the manuscript

claim: The global fit of the K267E variant is based on CPMG profiles of 33 residues.
source: The global fit of the K267E variant is based on CPMG profiles of 33 residues
evidence: CPMG relaxation dispersion NMR data from the manuscript

claim: The global fit of the R332A variant is derived from 18 residues.
source: while that of R332A is derived from 18 residues (Figure 3—figure supplements 2–4, Supplementary file 1).
evidence: CPMG relaxation dispersion NMR data from the manuscript with reference to supplementary figures

claim: Residues participating in the global motions of K267E and R332A variants are distinct from those of WT GeoRec2.
source: Interestingly, the residues participating in the global motions of both variants are distinct from those of WT GeoRec2, demonstrating that residue-specific flexibility is redistributed throughout GeoRec2
evidence: CPMG relaxation dispersion NMR data from the manuscript

claim: The mutation-induced reshuffling of ps-ns motions is negligible (<∆S2>≤0.1).
source: Bond vector fluctuations on the ps-ns timescale are only locally altered, thus the mutation-induced reshuffling of these motions is negligible (<∆S2>≤0.1)
evidence: NMR order parameter data from the manuscript

claim: A 39nt RNA containing the 21 bp spacer sequence was selected for NMR binding studies.
source: To mitigate this issue, a 39nt RNA containing the 21 bp spacer sequence was selected for its ability to maintain the NMR signal while being long enough to interact fully with the Rec lobe, as suggested by prior structures (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Experimental design decision described in the manuscript with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 2

claim: The GeoRec-39nt RNA complex is 55.6 kDa.
source: When bound to GeoRec, this complex is 55.6 kDa
evidence: Calculated molecular weight of the complex

claim: The strongest chemical shift perturbations upon RNA binding are localized to the GeoRec2 subdomain.
source: The strongest chemical shift perturbations are localized to the GeoRec2 subdomain that interfaces with the RNA:DNA hybrid at the PAM distal end
evidence: NMR chemical shift perturbation data from the manuscript

claim: The Kd of GeoRec for 39nt RNA is 3.3 ± 1.5 µM as measured by MST.
source: Microscale thermophoresis (MST) experiments quantified the affinity of GeoRec for this RNA, producing a Kd = 3.3 ± 1.5 µM that is consistent with the concentration-dependent NMR chemical shift perturbations (Figure 5A).
evidence: MST experimental data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 5A

claim: A three-fold greater concentration of RNA was required to induce maximal structural and dynamic effects in K267E and R332A variants compared to WT GeoRec.
source: Our NMR data revealed that a three-fold greater concentration of RNA was required to induce the maximal structural and dynamic effects in the variants than is required for WT GeoRec (Figure 4A/C)
evidence: NMR titration data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 4A/C

claim: K267E GeoRec has a Kd of 7.2 ± 1.0 µM for 39nt RNA as measured by MST.
source: MST experiments showed statistically significant reductions in RNA affinity for the K267E and R332A constructs, relative to WT GeoRec, where K267E GeoRec produced a Kd = 7.2 ± 1.0 µM
evidence: MST experimental data from the manuscript

claim: R332A GeoRec has a Kd of 7.2 ± 1.5 µM for 39nt RNA as measured by MST.
source: and R332A GeoRec produced a Kd = 7.2 ± 1.5 µM (Figure 5B, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: MST experimental data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 5B

claim: The Tm of full-length WT GeoCas9 is approximately 60 °C.
source: The thermal unfolding midpoint of full-length WT GeoCas9 determined by CD is ~60 °C
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript

claim: K267E and R332A mutations do not change the Tm of apo full-length GeoCas9.
source: and the K267E and R332A mutations do not change the Tm of the apo protein (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: Upon RNP formation with full-length gRNA, the Tm of WT GeoCas9 increases to 73 °C.
source: Upon formation of an RNP (using a full-length gRNA), the Tm of WT GeoCas9 increases to 73 °C.
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript

claim: K267E GeoCas9 RNP has a Tm of 70 °C.
source: K267E GeoCas9 retains a similar Tm increase to 70 °C
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript

claim: R332A GeoCas9 forms a less stable RNP with a Tm of 61 °C.
source: while R332A GeoCas9 forms a less stable RNP with Tm of 61 °C.
evidence: CD spectroscopy data from the manuscript

claim: Multi-microsecond MD simulations revealed substantial changes in the dynamics of GeoCas9 mutants compared to WT.
source: Multi-microsecond simulations revealed substantial changes in the dynamics of the GeoCas9 mutants compared to the WT (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: MD simulation data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: Mutations in the REC domain significantly altered the dynamics of both the Rec and the adjacent HNH domains.
source: Specifically, we observed that mutations in the REC domain significantly altered the dynamics of both the Rec and the adjacent HNH (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: MD simulation data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: The number of protein-RNA contacts was significantly reduced in all GeoCas9 variants compared to WT.
source: The number of contacts was significantly reduced in all variants compared to the WT, with the most pronounced reduction observed in the K267E variant (Figure 6C).
evidence: MD simulation data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 6C

claim: K267E GeoCas9 variant exhibited a substantial reduction in gRNA binding free energy (>60 kcal mol–1) relative to WT.
source: Consistent with a reduction in gRNA contacts, variants with the K267E mutation exhibited a substantial reduction in binding free energy (>60 kcal mol–1) relative to the WT
evidence: MM-GBSA binding free energy calculation from MD simulations

claim: R332A GeoCas9 variant displayed a smaller reduction in gRNA binding free energy (<20 kcal mol–1) compared to WT.
source: whereas the R332A variant displayed a smaller reduction (<20 kcal mol–1, Figure 6D).
evidence: MM-GBSA binding free energy calculation from MD simulations with reference to Figure 6D

claim: Protein-DNA interactions remained largely unaffected by K267E and R332A mutations.
source: Notably, protein-DNA interactions remained largely unaffected, suggesting that these mutations do not impair GeoCas9 DNA cleavage ability.
evidence: MD simulation data from the manuscript

claim: K267E and R332A mutations slightly diminished on-target DNA cleavage by GeoCas9, but the effect was very subtle.
source: Although the K267E and R332A mutations slightly diminished on-target DNA cleavage by GeoCas9, the effect was very subtle and these overall cleavage activities followed the temperature dependence of WT GeoCas9 quite closely (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: In vitro DNA cleavage assay data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 1

claim: WT GeoCas9 was increasingly sensitive to mismatched target sequences closer to the seed site.
source: As expected, WT GeoCas9 was increasingly sensitive to mismatched target sequences closer to the seed site, which has been demonstrated with SpyCas9 and other Cas systems (Harrington et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2016; Jinek et al., 2012; Hou et al., 2013).
evidence: In vitro off-target cleavage assay data from the manuscript, supported by citations to prior work

claim: A 1-minute digestion is sufficient for in vitro activity of GeoCas9 with the target DNA template.
source: No significant differences in activity were observed with digestion durations ranging from 1 to 60 min (Harrington et al., 2017), implying that a 1-min digestion is sufficient for in vitro activity of GeoCas9 with the target DNA template.
evidence: In vitro DNA cleavage assay data from the manuscript, supported by citation to prior work (Harrington et al., 2017)

claim: WT GeoCas9 showed nearly 50% cleavage for off-target DNA with a mismatch 5–6 base pairs from the PAM.
source: Specifically, a previous study reported ~10% cleavage of off-target DNA with a mismatch 5–6 base pairs from the PAM by WT GeoCas9 (Harrington et al., 2017). Our results showed nearly 50% cleavage for the same off-target mismatch
evidence: In vitro off-target cleavage assay data from the manuscript, compared to prior work (Harrington et al., 2017)

claim: K267E and R332A single-point mutants have negligible impact on GeoCas9 specificity.
source: Single-point mutants K267E and R332A GeoCas9 have negligible impact on GeoCas9 specificity (both variants follow the trend of WT GeoCas9, Figure 7—figure supplement 2)
evidence: In vitro off-target cleavage assay data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 2

claim: The K267E/R332A double mutant exhibits decreased on-target cleavage efficiency.
source: Additionally, a GeoCas9 double mutant K267E/R332A exhibits decreased on-target cleavage efficiency, which has been noted in high-specificity Cas systems (Chen et al., 2017; Slaymaker et al., 2016; Vakulskas et al., 2018; Casini et al., 2018; Kleinstiver et al., 2016; Hu et al., 2018; Lee et al., 2018).
evidence: In vitro DNA cleavage assay data from the manuscript, supported by citations to prior work

claim: The K267E/R332A double mutant does not enhance GeoCas9 specificity.
source: However, the additive effect of the K267E/R332A double mutant still does not enhance GeoCas9 specificity in our assay.
evidence: In vitro off-target cleavage assay data from the manuscript

claim: Full-length WT, K267E, and R332A GeoCas9 have similar affinities for Tnnt2 gRNA as measured by MST.
source: MST-derived binding affinities using full-length Tnnt2 gRNA and full-length WT, K267E, or R332A GeoCas9 indicate that all three proteins have similar affinities for the gRNA used in the functional assays (Figure 7).
evidence: MST experimental data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 7

claim: Mutations do not substantially alter full-length GeoCas9 binding to Tnnt2 gRNA.
source: Thus, mutations do not substantially alter full-length GeoCas9 binding to Tnnt2 gRNA, supporting similar cleavage activities for these proteins.
evidence: MST experimental data from the manuscript

claim: All GeoCas9 variants exhibited comparable affinities for the 8UZA gRNA sequence.
source: We repeated the MST experiments using a different gRNA sequence derived from the new cryo-EM structure of GeoCas9 (PDB:8UZA), which has a different spacer sequence. We observed a similar trend, as all GeoCas9 variants exhibited comparable affinities for this gRNA.
evidence: MST experimental data from the manuscript

source: GeoCas9 is a 1087 amino acid polypeptide
evidence: Basic protein information stated in the manuscript

source: The GeoRec2 domain from PDB: 8JTR (gray) is overlaid with our X-ray structure of GeoRec2 (red, PDB: 9B72).

source: Three-dimensional correlations and assignments were made in CARA (Keller, 2005) and GeoRec1 and GeoRec2 backbone assignments were deposited in the BMRB under accession numbers 52363

claim: iGeoCas9 contains 10 mutations (D8A, E149G, T182I, N206D, P466Q, H582A, Q817R, E843K, E854G, K908R).
source: Subsequently, we performed MD simulation of iGeoCas9 (PDB: 8UZB, resolution 2.63 Å) consisting of 10 mutations (D8A, E149G, T182I, N206D, P466Q, H582A, Q817R, E843K, E854G, K908R).

claim: iGeoCas9 exhibited increased dynamics in the HNH and Rec domains.
source: Intriguingly, iGeoCas9 exhibited increased dynamics in the HNH and Rec domains
evidence: MD simulation data from the manuscript

claim: iGeoCas9 showed a reduction in gRNA binding free energy similar to K267E and R332A mutants.
source: along with a reduction in gRNA binding free energy similar to the K267E and R332A mutants.
evidence: MD simulation data from the manuscript

claim: iGeoCas9 samples the greatest conformational space of any variant tested.
source: In fact, iGeoCas9 samples the greatest conformational space of any variant tested (Figure 6—figure supplement 1)
evidence: MD simulation data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 6—figure supplement 1

claim: High flexibility is critical to enhanced specificity in GeoCas9.
source: suggesting a high level of flexibility is critical to enhanced specificity in GeoCas9.
evidence: Inference drawn from MD simulation data comparing iGeoCas9 to other variants

claim: HiFi-SpyCas9 showed lower percent of digested off-target DNA sequences compared to WT SpyCas9.
source: As a control for on- and off-target activity, we assayed WT SpyCas9 alongside the widely used high-specificity HiFi-SpyCas9 variant (Vakulskas et al., 2018; Figure 7—figure supplement 2, Supplementary file 4) and found a lower percent of digested off-target (mismatched) DNA sequences when compared to WT SpyCas9.
evidence: In vitro off-target cleavage assay data from the manuscript with reference to Figure 7—figure supplement 2

claim: The biophysical impact of mutations within GeoRec2 and GeoRec may be tempered by its evolutionary resilience and the highly stable neighboring domains.
source: The biophysical impact of mutations within GeoRec2 and GeoRec may be tempered by its evolutionary resilience and the highly stable neighboring domains in the context of full-length GeoCas9
evidence: Speculation based on the observed functional data

claim: A greater number of additive or synergistic mutations within GeoRec would be required to fine-tune activity or specificity to a large degree.
source: Thus, a greater number of additive (or synergistic) mutations within GeoRec would be required to fine-tune activity or specificity to a large degree.
evidence: Speculation based on the observed functional data
